To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we introduce the forensic learning problem, 2) we present a new algorithm that is guaranteed to build the cheapest possible decision tree that satisfies a given level of classification accuracy, 3) our algorithm can be used to build a more efficient Clarify classifier that reduces total feature costs by many orders of magnitudes while only slightly reducing classification accuracy.

we introduce the forensic problem setting, present an information theoretic algorithm that is well-suited to the problem setting, and show that the algorithm is effective for building classifiers for real-world applications.
we have developed a new decision tree algorithm that can be used to build classifiers that maximize classification accuracy while minimizing the cost of acquiring the data for classification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of algorithms for building decision trees for forensic classification.
the problem of building classifiers with low total cost while maintaining high classification accuracy, and we demonstrate that the forensic classification problem is well suited for this task.
the design of algorithms that learn from experience in a cost-sensitive environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our algorithm can be used to build cheaper trees for the forensic classification problem.

our approach is able to build classifiers that are more cost-effective than existing techniques, and that this cost effectiveness is achieved at the expense of only a small decrease in classification accuracy.
we introduce a new cost-sensitive decision tree algorithm that is applicable to the forensic classification problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a new cost-sensitive decision tree algorithm, which we show to be effective in a real-world system.

our cost-sensitive learning algorithm can be used for building decision trees with lower computational cost, and hence, it can be used in situations where computational cost is an important consideration.
our algorithm is able to build cheaper decision trees than the existing methods for a given classification accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for some applications, the cost of building a classifier is a more important consideration than its accuracy.
cost-sensitive learning is a viable and effective technique for reducing the overhead of forensic classification systems.
the choice of learning algorithm can have a significant impact on the cost and accuracy of a classifier.
